title: Rheumatologist visit
what: A doctor who treats inflammatory conditions of the joints, spine, and connective tissue.
why: For joint pain, swelling, and stiffness, especially in the morning, or abnormal inflammation tests.
tell_doctor: Which joints hurt, and how long morning stiffness lasts
Any joint swelling or redness, rash, or fever
What medicines you take, including painkillers

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Bring blood tests and joint X-rays, if you had them.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that makes it easy to show the joints of your hands and feet.

bring: Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
Your joints are examined and felt
Test results and scans are reviewed
feel: Feeling sore joints may be unpleasant
Tell the doctor if it hurts. They will be more careful
after: Treatment is often long-term. Do not stop it on your own
red_flags: Severe joint swelling with a high fever: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: How is a rheumatologist different from an orthopedist?
faq.a: A rheumatologist treats joint inflammation with medicines. An orthopedist treats injuries and joint wear, often with surgery.
Any you have had: a blood count, sed rate, C-reactive protein. The doctor will order what is needed.

reminders.text: Rheumatologist visit tomorrow. Bring your test results and joint X-rays.
